The All-in-One Solution for Pet Owners

Project Overview

Furever Family is a pet care app that helps pet owners manage their pets' needs: booking grooming and vet appointments, buying pet supplies, managing schedules and getting emergency support.

Role
UX research and UI design, end to end
Platform
iOS mobile app
Research
Survey, 8 interviews, competitor audit, affinity map
Tools
Figma

Project Goal

Problem Statement

Pet owners and animal lovers struggle to get immediate veterinary help, ambulances or rescue services. The lack of a unified platform leads to delays and unreliable experiences, risking the health and safety of pets.

53.8%take their pet to the vet only when it's sick
60%can't keep track of vaccinations easily
65%still book vet appointments by phone call

From my survey of pet parents in Pune.

What do pet owners & vets truly need?

To understand the problem better, I spoke with pet parents, service providers and vets through interviews and surveys. This uncovered three major challenges.

Pet+
Care

01

Pet parents panic during emergencies and get confused by conflicting online information.

02

Vets lose clients due to scattered scheduling, no visibility and missed follow-ups.

03

Pet services like groomers, hostels and walkers are hard to trust, compare or book.

AffinityMapping

Affinity mapping showed that users want easy navigation, efficient features and solutions to common problems, all aimed at a better overall experience.

1Pet Parents Needs and Goals
Health and medical
Needs guidance on food, vaccination and training.Options for pet insurance to avoid unexpected high medical costs.Wants to offer personalised advice that online stores can't provide.
Grooming and personal care
Wants to provide a safe, home-like environment for pets.Reliable dog walkers and pet hostels when travelling or during late working hours.Hopes to expand and collaborate with vets and groomers.Hopes to expand into grooming and vet tie-ups.Aims to build trust with pet parents through reliable service.
Community & Reviews
Looking for a trustworthy community of pet parents for advice.Aims to build a strong community of pet parents.Gain positive reviews and referrals to strengthen reputation.
2Pet Parents Pain Points
Health and medical challenges
Finds it hard to track vaccination schedules.No easy access to after-hours or emergency vet care.Long waiting times at clinics even after appointments.
Grooming and personal care
Doesn't trust random trainers or groomers from apps, online or websites.Worries about Labrador's weight and health due to irregular exercise.Seasonal demand spikes (festivals, vacations) make space and staff management difficult.
Market challenges
Losing sales to online marketplaces due to discounts.Difficulty keeping up with new pet care products.Struggles with inventory management and digital adoption.
3Community
Community ideas
Awareness campaigns for preventive care.Community-driven events (training, workshops, meetups).Platform for adoption listings.Connecting new pet parents with experienced ones.
4Seasonal / Situational Needs
Seasonal needs
Emergency alerts during monsoon, summer or festivals.Travel and boarding surge management.Seasonal health tips and vaccinations.Adoption trends and awareness drives.Firecracker and festival alerts.

ResearchFindings

Pet Parents

01

Pet parents rely heavily on Google, YouTube and WhatsApp groups for advice, but the information is often conflicting or unreliable.

02

Most pet parents forget vaccination dates and follow-ups.

03

Emergencies cause panic, and parents struggle to find nearby, available vets quickly.

04

Finding trustworthy groomers, walkers or hostels is hard without verified reviews.

05

Community support exists, but it's disorganised and not guided by experts.

06

Medical records are scattered across paper, WhatsApp images and verbal instructions, making pet health hard to track.

Private Vet

01

Vets spend too much time on manual scheduling, calls and WhatsApp messages.

02

Medical histories are scattered, making diagnoses and follow-ups harder.

03

Vets face no-shows and last-minute cancellations that affect their workflow.

04

New or independent vets struggle with visibility and building a stable client base.

05

Collaboration with groomers, hostels and trainers is unstructured.

Personas

Pet Parents ↗

Rohan Sharma

Rohan is a 22-year-old motion designer living alone in Pune. He balances long work hours with caring for his Labrador, Leo, taking short breaks to play with him through the day. In the evenings he walks Leo and talks to nearby pet parents for advice. As a first-time pet parent he often relies on the internet for guidance, but conflicting information leaves him confused and stressed.

Private Vet ↗

Dr. Arjun

Dr. Arjun is a 28-year-old mobile veterinarian based in Pune, managing home visits for vaccinations, check-ups and minor treatments. His days are packed with travel, calls and scattered client information. He loves treating pets but struggles with missed follow-ups, last-minute cancellations and the lack of a simple digital system to manage his practice.

EmpathyMapping

Rohan Sharma

Says
  • My pet is like my child.
  • I wish there was one place for all pet-related needs.
  • I want trusted advice, not random Google searches.
  • I like to take my dog for a walk.
  • It's so hard to keep track of vaccinations.
Thinks
  • Am I giving my pet the best possible care?
  • What if I forget something important, like a vaccination?
  • Will this vet or hostel really treat my pet well?
  • Other pet parents probably know more than I do.
Does
  • Calls vets directly or uses WhatsApp to book.
  • Joins pet communities on WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram.
  • Relies on friends or online forums for advice.
  • Keeps paper vaccination cards or notes on his phone.
Feels
  • Love & attachment: pets are family.
  • Worry about health issues, emergencies and travel.
  • Frustration: services are scattered, trusted info is missing.
  • Overwhelmed by responsibilities and reminders.

Dr. Arjun

Says
  • Pet parents often come too late, only in emergencies.
  • Most owners forget vaccinations and regular check-ups.
  • I spend so much time managing calls and scheduling.
  • People rely on Google instead of asking a professional.
Thinks
  • How can I build trust so clients come back regularly?
  • I need more visibility to grow my practice.
  • I don't want to lose time with no-shows or cancellations.
  • Digital apps could help, but I don't want them complicated.
Does
  • Spends time on calls and WhatsApp scheduling appointments.
  • Educates owners about nutrition and preventive care.
  • Sometimes runs workshops or awareness sessions.
  • Takes payment after treating the pet.
Feels
  • Frustrated when owners skip preventive care.
  • Concerned about pets arriving in critical condition.
  • Satisfied seeing long-term healthy pets.
  • Motivated to educate owners and grow his practice.

KeyInsights

Each insight below shows the feature I designed in response. One is still open.

01

Trust is the biggest missing factor

Designed: Verified Vet badges, and a vet inside every Pet Group.
02

Information is scattered across platforms

Designed: Home dashboard with reminders, meals and pet profiles.
03

Pet parents need expert-backed content

Designed: Pet Library of vet-reviewed articles and videos.
04

Vets need digital support as much as pet parents

Still open: a vet-side scheduling view is not designed yet.
05

Communication between vets and pet parents breaks down easily

Designed: Ask a Vet: message a verified vet by speciality.
06

Community exists, but not structured

Designed: Pet Groups by breed and area, each guided by a vet.
07

One platform can solve multiple pain points

Designed: Five-tab bar: Home, Vets, Care, SOS, Community.
08

Emergencies expose the biggest gaps

Designed: SOS: swipe to book an ambulance from any screen.

SOS Screen

Four steps from panic to an ambulance.

Emergency support was the first project goal. SOS sits in the bottom bar of every screen, and a swipe, not a tap, confirms the booking so it can't be triggered by accident.

Swipe to book ambulance →SOS

StoryBoarding

Meet Priya. She's worried because her dog has been behaving oddly, and as a first-time pet parent she feels confused and alone. Here's how she handles it with the Furever Family app.

What'sNext

Test the SOS flow

Run a moderated usability test with 5 pet parents. Measure time from opening the app to a booked ambulance, and whether anyone triggers it by mistake.

Design the vet side

Insight 04 is still open. Dr. Arjun needs a scheduling and records view so reminders and follow-ups reach him too.

Measure trust

Track how often users act on Ask a Vet answers instead of going back to Google, and how often they rebook the same vet.
